result.narrative:
Boeing presents as a large, operationally strained but financially well-supported buyer. There are no open overdue notifications: the entire payment file is a single $650k invoice resolved 3 days late in June 2026, reported by one policyholder, with no accumulation in the prior 6-month window. Recent news flow is two-sided. On the adverse side sit a confirmed 5% cut to the commercial-airplane workforce, a further statement leaving more layoffs open, and a persistent production-constraint theme: 737 Max ramp-up deferred to late 2027, Max 10 certification delayed by a software issue, and a Transportation Department watchdog audit of FAA oversight. On the positive side, the backlog has grown to $745B, the $20B F/A-XX Navy award went uncontested, a $12B aircraft sale was announced, September deliveries ticked up to 57 jets, and the FAA cleared the 737 Max software glitch as not a flight-safety issue.

The score of 27.8 places the buyer in Watch, and it is driven entirely by news: 0.65 x 0.0 (payment, 0 DPD) + 0.35 x 79.5 (news) = 27.8. The adjudicator agreed with caveats. They confirmed the band is robust, because the next-ranked item is the confirmed 5% workforce cut at the same severity 4 with a decayed value of 77.9, only marginally below the 79.5 actually used, so removing the headline driver would not move the buyer out of Watch. But they flagged three things the underwriter should weigh: the article setting the score is speculative and body-less, scored at the same severity as the executed cut, so the headline 27.8 is inflated; the 0.0 payment input carries 65% of the weight yet rests on a file the review itself marks "insufficient_history", making it an absence of data rather than demonstrated good behaviour; and the formula uses only the single worst article, so the more durable production and certification cluster never aggregates while the material credit-positive evidence ($745B backlog, the Navy award, the aircraft sale, the FAA clearance) is scored 0.0 and cannot offset anything.

The recommendation is to maintain the one line in force: TCI's $9,000,000 export limit for Tamrin Exports, no change, with nothing currently owed. The probability of default of 0.1784 is within the 0.25 appetite threshold, maximum liability does not bind, and expected loss is unchanged at $1,156,032 before and after. Given the thin payment file, the sensible condition on approval is monitoring rather than a limit cut: the $9M line was last reviewed in April 2026 and the single resolved event is too slight to evidence a trend in either direction.

A move down to Healthy requires 7.8 points, which would come from the news side as the current severity-4 items decay against a 365-day half-life, provided the payment record stays at 0 DPD and no new adverse article replaces them. Confirmation that the speculative layoff item does not convert into further announced cuts, together with evidence that the 737 Max ramp-up and Max 10 certification are back on track, would remove the operational-distress theme the adjudicator identified as genuine. Building a fuller payment history across more than one policyholder would also raise confidence in the 0.0 input that currently carries most of the weight.
